# Volume 4 — CHAPTER 8 MISS WINIFRED TOLLEY COMES TO CALL

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

At Seven Gulls Harbor, that September brought golden mists and purple hazes—it was a month filled with sun-drenched days and nights that either swam in moonlight or pulsated with stars. Not a single storm ruined it, nor did any harsh wind blow. Nell and Hugh readied their home, wandered along the beaches, navigated the harbor, took drives around Seven Gulls and the Glen, or traveled along the fern-lined, secluded roads in the woods surrounding the harbor head; to put it briefly, they enjoyed a honeymoon that could have made any lovers anywhere jealous.
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0000 }

“If existence was to come to a sudden end right now it would nevertheless have been thoroughly worthwhile, merely on account of these previous four weeks, wouldn’t it?” spoken by Nell. “I do not imagine we shall ever enjoy four so flawless weeks again—yet we HAVE possessed them. All things—wind, weather, people, house of dreams—have joined together to render our honeymoon enchanting. There has not so much as been a wet day since our arrival here.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0001 }

“And we haven’t fought a single time,” Hugh joked.
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0002 }

“Indeed, ‘when a delight is postponed, its enjoyment is only amplified,’” recited Nell. “It brings me such joy that this location was chosen for our honeymoon. Rather than being dispersed across unfamiliar spots, the recollections we create will permanently reside right here, within our house of dreams.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0003 }

In the air of her new dwelling place, Nell discovered a particular flavor of romance and adventure that had always been absent in Brierley. While she had resided within view of the ocean in her former home, it had never been a close part of her daily existence. At Seven Gulls, however, she was enveloped by it, and it summoned her without ceasing. A different face of the water met her gaze from each window of the house. She continually heard its persistent, gentle hum. On a daily basis, ships navigated up the harbor toward the Glen wharf, or departed amidst the setting sun, heading for destinations that could be located on the opposite side of the world. Each morning, white-sailed fishing vessels glided down the waterway, coming back filled with their catch when night fell. Cheerful and satisfied mariners and fishing people walked along the twisting, red roads of the harbor. One constantly felt that events were about to unfold—that journeys and adventures lay just ahead. Life in Seven Gulls was far less quiet, established, and routine than in Brierley; breezes of transformation swept across the area; the ocean forever beckoned to the people living on the coast, and even the ones who could not respond to its summons experienced its excitement, agitation, secret nature, and endless potential.
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0004 }

“I comprehend now the reason certain men are compelled to head to sea,” remarked Nell. “That longing that strikes every one of us occasionally—‘to sail beyond the bourne of sunset’—is surely immensely commanding when someone is born with it. It does not surprise me that Captain Saul escaped on account of it. Whenever I spot a vessel gliding out of the channel, or a seagull gliding above the sand-bar, I invariably wish that I was aboard that vessel or possessed wings, not in the manner of a dove ‘to fly away and be at rest,’ but in the manner of a seagull, to dart straight into the absolute center of a tempest.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0005 }

“Nell-girl, you will remain right here beside me,” Hugh stated in a relaxed manner. “Flying off into the centers of tempests and away from me is something I will not permit you to do.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0006 }

Their position in the late afternoon was upon their red sand-stone doorstep. Land, sea, and sky enveloped them in great tranquillities. Soaring above them were silvery gulls. Long trails of frail, pinkish clouds laced the horizons. A murmurous refrain of minstrel winds and waves threaded the hushed air. In the sere and misty meadows that lay between them and the harbor, pale asters were blowing.
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0007 }

“Medical men forced to remain awake through the night attending to the ill are not apt to possess a strong sense of adventure, I imagine,” Nell remarked with tolerance. “Had you enjoyed a restful sleep yesterday evening, Hugh, your eagerness for an excursion of fancy would match my own.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0008 }

“I performed good work during the night, Nell,” Hugh said softly. “With God’s help, I preserved a life. It is the very first instance I could truly make that claim. In different situations I might have assisted; however, Nell, had I failed to remain at Allonby’s during the night and battle death directly, that woman must have perished prior to morning. I attempted a trial that was surely never attempted in Seven Gulls previously. I question whether it was ever attempted anywhere previously beyond a hospital. It was a recent method in Portmaris hospital this past winter. I could not ever have ventured to attempt it here had I not been completely sure that no other hope existed. I took the risk—and it worked. Consequently, a fine wife and mother is preserved for many years of joy and utility. When I traveled home earlier today, as the sun ascended above the harbor, I offered thanks to God for picking the career that I picked. I had waged a fine battle and triumphed—consider it, Nell, TRIUMPHED, against the Great Destroyer. It is the thing I envisioned accomplishing in the past when we conversed with each other about our desires for life. That vision of mine turned into reality earlier today.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0009 }

“Did any of your other dreams end up becoming reality?” inquired Nell, fully aware of what he would reply, yet desiring to listen to it once more.
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0010 }

“IT is clear to you, Nell-girl,” Hugh remarked, a smile meeting her gaze. Just then, a pair of utterly joyful individuals were undoubtedly seated upon the front step belonging to a small, white dwelling along the margin of Seven Gulls Harbor.
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0011 }

A moment later, Hugh spoke, his voice shifting, “Am I mistaken, or is a full-rigged ship making its way up our lane?”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0012 }

Nell looked and sprang up.
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0013 }

“That is surely either Mrs. Vane or Miss Winifred Tolley arriving for a visit,” she remarked.
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0014 }

“I shall step inside the office, and I give you warning that if Miss Winifred is there, I will listen in,” Hugh remarked. “Based on everything I have been told about Miss Winifred, I gather her talk is bound to be anything but uninteresting.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0015 }

“Perhaps it is Mrs. Vane.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0016 }

“Mrs. Vane does not strike me as being constructed in that manner. Recently, I observed her tending to her garden, and despite being at too great a distance for a distinct view, my impression was that she appeared quite slim. Given that she has failed to pay you a visit so far, despite her status as your closest neighbor, she does not appear particularly disposed toward socializing.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0017 }

“Unless curiosity brought her, she cannot resemble Mrs. Sowerby,” Nell remarked. “Miss Winifred is who I believe this visitor to be.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0018 }

It was indeed Miss Winifred; furthermore, Miss Winifred had not arrived to execute a short and stylish nuptial visit. Her work was cradled beneath her arm inside a solid bundle, and upon Nell’s invitation to remain, she immediately removed her large sun-hat, which a firm elastic band beneath the rigid, tiny bun of her blonde hair had secured to her head, notwithstanding the impudent September gusts. No hat pins were suited for Miss Winifred, if you please! Elastic bands had served her mother sufficiently well, and they served HER sufficiently well. A healthy, circular, pink-and-white complexion belonged to her, alongside cheerful brown eyes. The conventional old maid was not reflected in her appearance at all, and a quality in her countenance captured Nell immediately. Utilizing her long-standing, intuitive speed at identifying like-minded people, she recognized that she would come to fondle Miss Winifred, regardless of unpredictable peculiarities of belief, and undeniable peculiarities of dress.
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0019 }

Except for Miss Winifred, no one would have arrived to pay a visit dressed in a blue-and-white striped apron alongside a chocolate print wrapper adorned with a pattern of giant, dispersed pink roses. Furthermore, no one except Miss Winifred was capable of appearing stately and appropriately dressed while wearing such attire. If Miss Winifred had been stepping into a royal residence to visit the bride of a prince, her dignity and absolute command of the circumstances would have remained entirely unchanged. She would have dragged her rose-covered ruffle across the marble flooring with equal indifference, and she would have moved forward with identical composure to rid the princess's thoughts of any belief that owning a simple man, whether a prince or a peasant, was something to boast about.
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0020 }

“My task has come along with me, dear Mrs. Carrow,” she observed, spreading out a piece of delicate fabric. “Finishing this quickly is my priority, and not a single moment can be wasted.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0021 }

Nell observed the white piece of clothing laid across Miss Winifred’s spacious lap with a degree of astonishment. Unquestionably, it was an infant's gown, and it possessed magnificent craftsmanship featuring minute tucks and frills. Positioning her spectacles, Miss Winifred commenced sewing with extraordinarily fine stitches.
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0022 }

“This is intended for Mrs. Gideon Proctor up at the Glen,” she declared. “Any day now, she is anticipating the birth of her eighth baby, and she does not have a single stitch prepared for it. Whatever she crafted for the first child has been worn out by the subsequent seven, and she has lacked the time, energy, or heart to craft any more. Mark MY words, Mrs. Carrow, that woman is a martyr. I foresaw the outcome the moment she wed Gideon Proctor. He belonged to that class of evil, captivating men. Once married, his captivating nature vanished, leaving only his evil ways behind. He consumes alcohol and ignores his household. Is that not typical of a man? Without the assistance of her neighbors, I have no idea how Mrs. Proctor would manage to keep her children respectably dressed.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0023 }

Miss Winifred, as Nell would discover later on, stood alone among the neighbors in concerning herself with the proper conduct of the young Proctors.
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0024 }

“I made up my mind to craft a few items for this eighth child upon learning it was on the way,” Miss Winifred continued. “I am aiming to complete this final one today.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0025 }

“It is without a doubt extremely lovely,” Nell remarked. “I am going to fetch my needlework so the two of us can hold a small sewing gathering. Miss Tolley, your skill at stitching is marvelous.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0026 }

“Indeed, I am the top needlewoman around here,” stated Miss Winifred with a straightforward demeanor. “It is only natural! My goodness, I have sewn more than I would have if I had birthed a hundred offspring myself, you can take my word for it! I guess I am silly, adorning this garment for an eighth child with manual needlework. However, goodness, Mrs. Carrow, my dear, the child is not at fault for being number eight, and I sort of wanted it to possess a single genuinely lovely gown, exactly as though it WERE desired. No one wants the unfortunate little creature—hence I added additional detail to its small garments for that very reason.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0027 }

“That dress is something any baby could take pride in,” remarked Nell, experiencing an even deeper conviction that Miss Winifred would be to her liking.
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0028 }

“I imagine you’ve been under the impression that I would never drop by to visit you,” Miss Winifred continued. “However, this happens to be the harvest season, as you are aware, and I’ve been occupied—plus there are numerous additional laborers idling about, consuming more food than the labor they perform, precisely like the men. I would have paid a visit yesterday, except I attended the funeral of Mrs. Roderick MacAllister. Initially, I believed my head was throbbing so severely that I wouldn’t be able to enjoy myself even if I attended. Nevertheless, she had reached a hundred years of age, and I had consistently vowed to myself that I would be present at her funeral.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0029 }

“Did the event go well?” Nell inquired, seeing that the door to the office stood slightly open.
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0030 }

“What is that? Ah, indeed, the funeral was enormous. Her circle of acquaintances was extensive. More than one hundred and twenty carriages joined the procession. A couple of amusing incidents occurred. I believed I would expire from laughter upon witnessing old Joe Bradshaw, an infidel who refuses to enter a church, passionately and fervently belt out 'Safe in the Arms of Jesus’. Singing is his pride and joy—for that reason, he attends every single funeral. Poor Mrs. Bradshaw appeared far from singing—completely exhausted from endless toil. Occasionally, old Joe sets off intending to purchase a gift for her, only to return with a different piece of agricultural equipment. Does that not epitomize a man? Yet what other behavior could one anticipate from a male who avoids church entirely, even a Methodist chapel? It gave me genuine gratitude to spot you alongside the young Doctor attending the Presbyterian church on your inaugural Sunday. I refuse to be treated by any doctor who fails to be a Presbyterian.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0031 }

“Last Sunday evening, we attended the Methodist church,” Nell stated mischievously.
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0032 }

“Well, I reckon Dr. Carrow must attend the Methodist church occasionally, otherwise he would lose the Methodist practice.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0033 }

“The sermon was very much to our liking,” Nell stated courageously. “And in my opinion, the prayer from the Methodist minister was among the most exquisite I have ever listened to.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0034 }

“Oh, there is no question in my mind that he is capable of praying. No one ever produced more lovely prayers in my hearing than old Simon Bentley, who remained perpetually intoxicated, or longed to become so, and his praying improved the more intoxicated he became.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0035 }

“The Methodist preacher possesses a most handsome appearance,” remarked Nell, directing her words toward the office door.
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0036 }

“Indeed, he is rather decorative,” concurred Miss Winifred. “Oh, and EXTREMELY effeminate. Furthermore, he imagines that he enamors any young woman who glances his way—as though a itinerant Jewish-like Methodist clergyman were a great catch! Should you and the young doctor follow MY counsel, you will keep your distance from the Methodists. My principle remains—if you HAPPEN to be a Presbyterian, ACT like a Presbyterian.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0037 }

“Is it not your belief that Methodists reach heaven just like Presbyterians?” Nell inquired, without a smile.
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0038 }

“We are not the ones to make that decision. Higher powers hold it,” Miss Winifred declared gravely. “However, I refuse to mingle with them in this life, regardless of what might be required of me in the next. Unmarried is what THIS Methodist minister happens to be. Married was the previous one they possessed, and I never laid eyes on a creature more foolish and fickle than his spouse. That her husband ought to have delayed marrying her until her adulthood was a piece of advice I once offered him. His response was that he wished to guide her upbringing himself. Is that not just how a man thinks?”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0039 }

“It is quite difficult to determine the exact moment when individuals ARE adults,” Nell laughed.
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0040 }

“That’s accurate, dearie. Certain people are already mature at birth, whereas others haven't matured by the time they reach eighty, take MY word for it. The very same Mrs. Roderick I mentioned earlier did not ever mature. She remained just as silly at a hundred years old as she had been at ten.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0041 }

“It’s possible that explained her long life,” Nell offered.
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0042 }

“Perhaps it was. I would prefer to exist for fifty rational years instead of a hundred senseless ones.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0043 }

“Yet only consider how monotonous the world would become if all people were prudent,” begged Nell.
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0044 }

Miss Winifred held any contest of frivolous witticism in contempt.
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0045 }

“Mrs. Roderick belonged to the Milgrave family, and a great deal of sense was something the Milgraves never possessed. For a long period, her nephew, Ebenezer Milgrave, suffered from insanity. His delusion was that he had passed away, and he frequently flew into rages at his wife for refusing to inter him. I’d a-done it.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0046 }

Miss Winifred appeared so fiercely resolved that Nell was nearly able to picture her holding a spade.
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0047 }

“Are there NOT any good husbands you know, Miss Tolley?”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0048 }

“Oh, yes, lots of them—over yonder,” Miss Winifred said, gesturing with her hand out the open window in the direction of the small church graveyard situated across the harbor.
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0049 }

“Yet being alive—moving around in a body?” insisted Nell.
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0050 }

“Oh, to demonstrate that every single thing can be done through God, a handful exist,” Miss Winifred admitted unwillingly. “I will not dispute that a rare male scattered here or there might become a respectable creature, provided he is taken while young, raised correctly, and thoroughly disciplined by his mother in advance. YOUR husband, at present, is not terribly awful, compared to other men, based on everything I am told. I imagine”—Miss Winifred peered intently at Nell across her spectacles—“you believe no one else on earth compares to him.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0051 }

“There is not,” Nell replied without delay.
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0052 }

“Ah, well, I listened to a different bride express that on a past occasion,” Miss Winifred uttered with a sigh. “Upon her marriage, Jennie Dean believed that no one in existence compared to HER husband. Her assessment was correct—no such person existed! Furthermore, take MY word for it, that was fortunate! The existence he forced upon her was terrible—and as Jennie was on her deathbed, he was already pursuing his next spouse.
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0053 }

“Is that not typical of a man? Nevertheless, my hope is that YOUR faith proves more well-founded, dearie. The youth who is a doctor is catching on very well. My initial fear was that he might not, because the people in these parts have forever considered old Doctor Dave as the sole doctor anywhere. To be certain, Doctor Dave lacked much tact—he constantly brought up ropes in dwellings where a person had committed suicide. Yet people overlooked their injured sentiments whenever their stomachs pained them. Had he served as a minister rather than a doctor, forgiveness would never have been granted to him. A aching soul causes people far less concern than a aching stomach. Since the two of us are Presbyterians with no Methodists present, would you share with me your honest view regarding OUR minister?”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0054 }

“Why—really—I—well,” Nell stammered.
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0055 }

Miss Winifred gave a nod.
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0056 }

“Precisely. My sentiment aligns with yours, my dear. Calling HIM was an error on our part. Does his visage not resemble one of those elongated, slender headstones in the cemetery? His brow should be inscribed with 'Sacred to the memory.’ The initial discourse he delivered upon his arrival remains etched in my memory. The topic concerned each person engaging in the work for which they are best suited—undoubtedly an excellent topic; yet the examples he cited were astonishing! He remarked, 'If you had a cow and an apple tree, and if you tied the apple tree in your stable and planted the cow in your orchard, with her legs up, how much milk would you get from the apple tree, or how many apples from the cow?’ Have you ever encountered such a thing in all your life, my dear? It brought me great relief that no Methodists were present that day—their mockery would have been endless. However, my chief grievance regarding him is his tendency to concur with everyone, regardless of what is stated. Should you tell him, 'You’re a scoundrel,’ he would respond, accompanied by that bland grin, 'Yes, that’s so.’ A pastor ought to possess greater fortitude. Ultimately, I regard him as an ordained fool. Naturally, this remains strictly between the two of us. In the presence of Methodists, I laud him immensely. Certain individuals believe his spouse wears attire that is overly vibrant, yet my view is that cohabiting with a countenance like his warrants something to brighten her spirits. I will never be heard criticizing a female regarding her garments. My heart is simply grateful when her spouse is not so stingy and parsimonious as to forbid it. Not that I devote much attention to clothing personally. Females merely attire themselves to gratify males, and I would refuse to demean myself to THAT extent. My existence has been genuinely tranquil and pleasant, my dear, entirely because I never valued the opinions of men in the slightest.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0057 }

“What makes you despise the men to such a degree, Miss Tolley?”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0058 }

“Lord, honey, I lack hatred for them. They do not deserve it. I merely rather hold them in contempt. I believe I will care for YOUR husband should he persist in the manner he started. Yet except for him, the old doctor together with Captain Saul are nearly the sole men on earth I value at all.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0059 }

“To be sure, Captain Saul is marvelous,” Nell concurred warmly.
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0060 }

“Captain Saul is a decent chap, though he’s somewhat irritating in a single regard. You simply CANNOT get him angry. I’ve attempted it for two decades, yet he continues to remain calm. It rather annoys me, in a way. And I imagine the lady he ought to have wedded ended up with a spouse who flew into rages a couple of times daily.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0061 }

“What was her identity?”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0062 }

“Well, I am uncertain, my sweet. Captain Saul courting anyone is something I have no recollection of. As long as I can recall, he was getting on in years. As you are aware, seventy-six is his age. Why he remained unmarried was never explained to my knowledge, yet I assure YOU a cause exists. Up until five years back, he spent his whole existence at sea, exploring every single nook of the world. Throughout their existence, he and Elizabeth Russell maintained a deep friendship, yet romantic intentions were never present between them. Despite numerous opportunities, Elizabeth never wed. During her youth, her beauty was remarkable. Her uncle, a Government official residing in Port Marlow, hosted her as a guest during the year the Prince of Wales visited the Island, which led to her receiving a ball invitation. No girl present surpassed her in looks, leading the Prince to dance with her, an act that enraged every unchosen woman whose higher societal rank caused them to claim he ought not to have ignored them. That particular dance remained a point of immense pride for Elizabeth. Spiteful individuals claimed this explained her refusal to marry—that having danced with royalty, a common man would no longer suffice. That claim, however, was false. The true cause was once disclosed to me by her—she possessed such a fierce disposition that she feared peaceful cohabitation with any husband would be impossible. Indeed, her temper was terrible—occasionally, to control it, she was forced to retreat to her room above and sink her teeth into the furniture. Nevertheless, I informed her that such a flaw should not prevent her from wedlock if she desired it. We ought not to allow men to hold a monopoly on bad tempers, wouldn't you agree, my dear Mrs. Carrow?”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0063 }

“My own patience is somewhat short-lived,” Nell let out a sigh.
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0064 }

“It is good that you possess it, my dear. You will stand much less chance of being stepped upon, trust ME! Goodness, the way your golden glow is flourishing! The garden you have looks magnificent. Poor Elizabeth used to tend to it so meticulously.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0065 }

“I love it,” Nell said. “I’m happy it has so many old-fashioned flowers. Talking about gardening, we need to find someone to dig up that small plot past the fir grove and plant it with strawberry plants for us. Hugh is so occupied that he will not have time for it this autumn. Do you know of anybody we could hire?”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0066 }

“Indeed, Henry Rudge over at the Glen takes on those sorts of tasks. Perhaps he will suffice. He is forever far more concerned with his pay than his labor, precisely like a male, and he is so sluggish to comprehend that he remains motionless for five minutes prior to realizing he has halted. His father launched a log at him during his youth.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0067 }

“That was a lovely, soft rocket, wasn’t it? Just like a man would do! Naturally, the lad didn’t ever recover. Nevertheless, he is the single person I am able to endorse whatsoever. Last spring, he did the painting on my house. Don't you agree that it appears truly lovely at present?”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0068 }

It was the five o'clock chime of the clock that rescued Nell.
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0069 }

“My goodness, has it reached that hour already?” Miss Winifred cried out. “When a person is having fun, the hours really do fly! Oh well, I ought to head back to my house.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0070 }

“No, certainly not! You will remain and join us for tea,” Nell exclaimed enthusiastically.
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0071 }

“Do you inquire of me since you believe you must, or owing to your genuine desire?” inquired Miss Winifred.
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0072 }

“Since I truly desire to.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0073 }

“In that case, I shall remain. YOUR people are the ones who recognize Joseph.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0074 }

“I am certain that a friendship will form between us,” Nell remarked, accompanied by the specific expression that was revealed solely to those belonging to the household of faith.
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0075 }

“Indeed, we do, dearie. Thank heaven, selecting our friends is within our power. Our relatives must be accepted as they come, and we should be grateful when none of them are jailbirds. Not that I possess many—my closest are merely second cousins. Mrs. Carrow, I am somewhat of a solitary person.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0076 }

A tone of yearning was present in the voice of Miss Winifred.
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0077 }

“I want you to address me as Nell,” Nell blurted out with sudden emotion. “It would feel extra HOMEY that way. With the exception of my husband, all the people in Seven Gulls address me as Mrs. Carrow, which gives me the sensation of being an outsider. Were you aware that the name you have is almost identical to the single one I longed for as a little girl. I despised 'Nell’ and adopted 'Lucinda’ as my name in my mind.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0078 }

“I am fond of Nell. My mother was called that. In my view, traditional names are the finest and most charming. Should you be fetching tea, you could ask the young doctor to come speak with me. Since my arrival, he has been stretched out on the sofa in that office, chuckling uncontrollably at my remarks.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0079 }

“How did you know?” exclaimed Nell, who was far too shocked by this example of Miss Winifred’s weird foresight to offer a courteous disavowal.
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0080 }

“Upon walking up the path, I spotted him seated next to you, and I am well aware of how men behave,” Miss Winifred countered. “Well, I have completed my tiny garment, darling, and the arrival of the eighth child can happen whenever it wishes.”
{: #nw-v04-c08-p0081 }
